Q: How do I extract a valid command line(s) from a VS Code launch.json file? A:

You can use program jq to extract data from JSON file and reformat them

It gets all elements in list "configurations", joins elements in args to one string using space as separator,

  • next it creates list only with name and args (if there can be other values) and again it joins them to one string with space.
jq '.configurations[] | .args |= join(" ") | [.name, .args] | join(" ")' launch.json
  • or it formats string directly using values name, args
jq '.configurations[] | .args |= join(" ") | "\(.name) \(.args)"' launch.json

(char | means piping like in bash)

Result:

"myprog foo1 bar1 foo2 bar2 etc andsoon"
"other --text long text with spaces --hello world"

but (at this moment) it doesn't add quotation marks for arguments which have spaces.

With option -r (or --raw-output) it gives output without quotation marks

jq -r '.configurations[] | .args |= join(" ") | "\(.name) \(.args)"' launch.json

myprog foo1 bar1 foo2 bar2 etc andsoon
other --text long text with spaces --hello world

There is also --raw-output0 if you would need NUL instead newline after each output.

More in documentation

In comment @jonrsharpe shows simpler method with flatten if there is only name and args

jq -r '.configurations[] | flatten | join(" ")' launch.json

There is also link to The JQ Playground

json - Transform array to string using jq - Stack Overflow

json - Printing multiple values on the same line - Stack Overflow

Q: Javascript full stack A:

Your logic is actually fine. The problem is not the condition — it’s that your function is never being called (or not called at the right time).

Q: How to print variable non-recursively in GDB A:

Try this

p -max-depth 1 -- myvar

Q: Issues with comments on JSON file A:

Another great tool for this is fx (https://fx.wtf). It's designed for interactive processing of JSON on the command line and is more forgiving of things like comments by default. You can pipe your JSONC (JSON with comments) file directly to it.

If you need to enforce strict JSON validation, fx also includes a --strict flag.

# This will work with comments
cat my_json_with_comments.json | fx .

# This will fail if there are comments, enforcing strict JSON
cat my_json_with_comments.json | fx --strict .
